## Report: Skill Categorization Mechanism

Based on my exploration of both the local repo and upstream anthropics/skills, here's how categorization works:

### **Upstream Pattern: `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`**

The **anthropics/skills** repository uses a explicit categorization file at `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`:

```json
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "name": "document-skills",
      "description": "Collection of document processing suite...",
      "skills": [
        "./skills/xlsx",
        "./skills/docx",
        "./skills/pptx",
        "./skills/pdf"
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "example-skills",
      "description": "Collection of example skills...",
      "skills": [
        "./skills/algorithmic-art",
        "./skills/brand-guidelines",
        ...
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "claude-api",
      "description": "Claude API and SDK documentation...",
      "skills": ["./skills/claude-api"]
    }
  ]
}
```

This file:
- Groups individual skills into named **plugin collections** (e.g., "document-skills", "example-skills", "claude-api")
- Each collection has a `name`, `description`, and list of skill paths
- These categories appear in the `npx skills@latest add` CLI selection UI (as reported in your earlier observation of "Claude Api", "Document Skills", "Example Skills" groupings)

### **Current Repo Status**

This repo currently has **NO** categorization layer:

1. **Structure**: Skills are split into `skills/local/` and `skills/vendor/` (filesystem grouping only)
2. **vendor.yaml**: Tracks upstream sources with optional `series:` field (e.g., `series: fullstack-nextjs`) for subdirectory organization, **but this is only for filesystem layout**, not for user-facing category labels
3. **mkdocs.yml**: Uses hierarchical documentation organization (Local, Vendored, Fullstack Next.js subsection) **for docs only**—this does not affect the `npx skills` CLI discovery
4. **No marketplace metadata**: The repo lacks a `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` file or equivalent category manifest that the CLI would read

### **Concrete Recommendation**

**Create `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`** at the repo root with the following structure:

```json
{
  "name": "daviddwlee84-agent-skills",
  "owner": {
    "name": "David D. W. Lee"
  },
  "metadata": {
    "description": "Personal collection of agent skills",
    "version": "1.0.0"
  },
  "plugins": [
    {
      "name": "project-management",
      "description": "Project memory, TODO tracking, and development workflow organization",
      "source": "./",
      "strict": false,
      "skills": [
        "./skills/local/project-knowledge-harness",
        "./skills/local/agent-history-hygiene"
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "ml-ops",
      "description": "ML experiment tracking, DVC pipelines, and model workflow tools",
      "source": "./",
      "strict": false,
      "skills": [
        "./skills/local/mlflow-tracking",
        "./skills/local/dvc-ml-workflow",
        "./skills/local/marimo-batch-mlflow"
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "fullstack-nextjs-series",
      "description": "Full-stack web development: Next.js, Supabase, shadcn/ui, testing",
      "source": "./",
      "strict": false,
      "skills": [
        "./skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/nextjs",
        "./skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/supabase",
        "./skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/shadcn",
        "./skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/react-best-practices",
        "./skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/vercel-storage",
        "./skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/supabase-postgres-best-practices",
        "./skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/web-design-guidelines",
        "./skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/frontend-design",
        "./skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/webapp-testing"
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "authoring-and-docs",
      "description": "Skill creation, documentation generation, and content authoring",
      "source": "./",
      "strict": false,
      "skills": [
        "./skills/local/skill-author",
        "./skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap",
        "./skills/vendor/skill-creator"
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "notebooks-and-widgets",
      "description": "Interactive notebook environments and widget creation",
      "source": "./",
      "strict": false,
      "skills": [
        "./skills/vendor/marimo-notebook",
        "./skills/vendor/streamlit-to-marimo",
        "./skills/vendor/anywidget"
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "other",
      "description": "Specialized tools and utilities",
      "source": "./",
      "strict": false,
      "skills": [
        "./skills/local/quantatitive-factor-researcher",
        "./skills/local/pueue-job-queue"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Why this works:**
- The `npx skills@latest` CLI reads `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` to populate category groupings in its interactive selection UI
- Each plugin is a visible category tab/section in the selection interface
- The `series:` field in `vendor.yaml` remains useful for filesystem organization (to avoid `.` directory bloat)—it and `marketplace.json` complement each other

**Key differences from current setup:**
- `vendor.yaml` governs **source syncing**; `marketplace.json` governs **user-facing category discovery**
- Both can coexist; they serve different purposes

Sources:
- [anthropics/skills marketplace.json](https://github.com/anthropics/skills/blob/main/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json)
- [vercel-labs/skills (npx skills CLI)](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills)
- [Skills-CLI Guide on Medium](https://medium.com/@jacklandrin/skills-cli-guide-using-npx-skills-to-supercharge-your-ai-agents-38ddf3f0a826)

1	# Agent Skills
2	
3	A personal collection of [agent skills](https://agentskills.io/home) — both custom-authored and cherry-picked from upstream repos — installable as a single package.
4	
5	📚 **[Read the docs](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/)** for the full guide, conventions, and skill index.

7	## Install
8	
9	<!-- snippet:install (keep in sync with docs/_snippets/install.md) -->
10	```bash
11	npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills
12	```
13	
14	> **Note**
15	> The trailing `/skills` matters. Without it, `npx skills` will look in
16	> `.agents/skills/` of the upstream repo, which contains a different
17	> layout. The `skills/` suffix points the installer at the
18	> `skills/local/` and `skills/vendor/` trees.

49	## Repo memory
50	
51	This repo dogfoods `project-knowledge-harness` on itself:
52	
53	- [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) — priority/effort-tagged backlog.
54	- [`backlog/`](backlog/) — research notes for `P?` items (when populated).
55	- [`backlog/inbox.md`](backlog/) — quick-capture inbox; sweep into `TODO.md` later.
56	- [`pitfalls/`](pitfalls/) — symptom-grep-able knowledge base of past traps (when populated).
57	
58	```bash
59	# Validate TODO.md and render kanban-style board
60	make kanban
61	
62	# Quick add structured TODO entry
63	./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M --title "..." --description "..."
64	
65	# Move an active TODO to ## Done in same commit as the implementation
66	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<shipped summary>"
67	
68	# Triage backlog/inbox.md interactively
69	./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh
70	```
71	
72	Full workflow: [Project memory](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/workflows/project-memory/).
73	
74	## Vendor system
75	
76	```bash
77	# Add a vendored skill (auto-syncs)
78	./scripts/add-vendor.sh owner/repo/path/to/skill
79	# or via Makefile
80	make add-vendor SOURCE=owner/repo/path/to/skill
81	
82	# Group into a series subdir (skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/)
83	./scripts/add-vendor.sh --series fullstack-nextjs vercel/vercel-plugin/skills/nextjs
84	
85	# Sync all vendored skills from upstream
86	make sync
87	
88	# Check for upstream updates (dry-run)
89	make sync-check
90	```
91	
92	Full workflow: [Adding vendor skills](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/workflows/adding-vendor-skills/).
93	
94	**Dependencies:** `gh` (GitHub CLI, authenticated) and `yq` (YAML processor).
95	
96	## Docs site
97	
98	The docs site is built with MkDocs Material + `mkdocs-llmstxt` + `mkdocs-copy-to-llm`.
99	
100	```bash
101	uv sync --extra docs
102	make docs-serve         # http://127.0.0.1:8000/
103	make docs-build         # produces ./site/
104	```
105	
106	Deployed automatically to GitHub Pages on push to `main` via [`.github/workflows/docs.yml`](.github/workflows/docs.yml).
107	
108	If you want to apply the same docs stack to your own project, see [Downstream docs stack recipe](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/reference/docs-stack-recipe/).
109	
110	## Adding a new local skill
111	
112	Use the bundled scaffolder (recommended — seeds the agentskills.io best-practice template):
113	
114	```bash
115	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh <skill-name>
116	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh skills/local/<skill-name>
117	```
118	
119	Or with the upstream init:
120	
121	```bash
122	cd skills/local
123	npx skills@latest init [skill-name]
124	```
125	
126	See [Creating local skills](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/workflows/creating-local-skills/) for the layout rules and authoring guidance.

5	
6	# Skill Author
7	
8	Helps you write **new agent skills** that follow the best-practices documented at
9	https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/ — without you having to re-read those pages
10	every time. Pairs with `skill-creator` (which handles eval/iterate/optimize loops
11	once a draft exists).
12	
13	## When to use this vs `skill-creator`
14	
15	| Task | Use |
16	|---|---|
17	| "I want to make a new skill for X" | **skill-author** (scaffold + author) |
18	| "Scaffold the SKILL.md / a reference / a script" | **skill-author** |
19	| "Lint this skill draft" | **skill-author** |
20	| "My skill isn't triggering when I want it to" | `skill-creator` (description optimization) |
21	| "Run test cases against my skill, benchmark it" | `skill-creator` (eval loop) |
22	| "Compare two versions of my skill" | `skill-creator` (blind comparison) |
23	
24	If both apply, start here, then hand off to `skill-creator` once the draft is solid.
25	
26	## Workflow
27	
28	### 1. Capture intent (1 minute)
29	
30	Before scaffolding, get four answers — usually just by asking the user:
31	
32	1. **What does it do?** (one sentence)
33	2. **When should it trigger?** (specific user phrases / contexts)
34	3. **What does it output?** (file, command result, plan, prose)
35	4. **Is the output objectively verifiable?** (decides whether `skill-creator` evals are worth the effort later)
36	
37	Write these four down before touching files. They become the seeds for the
38	description, the workflow body, and the future eval set.
39	
40	### 2. Scaffold
41	
42	Use `scripts/new-skill.sh` to produce the directory layout:
43	
44	```bash
45	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh <skill-name>
46	# creates: skills/local/<skill-name>/{SKILL.md,references/,scripts/,assets/}
47	# seeds:   SKILL.md from assets/SKILL.md.template
48	```

I found relevant search results for the `skills` npm CLI tool. Here's what I discovered:

## Overview

The CLI is for the open agent skills ecosystem and supports OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and 49 more agents.

## Skill Categories and Organization

There's a directory called skills.sh that is a leaderboard for skill packages where you can discover new skills to enhance your agents, browse skills by category and popularity, and track usage stats and installs across the ecosystem.

## Key Commands

You can list installed skills with `npx skills list` or `npx skills ls`, filter by agent with `npx skills ls -a cursor`, search the registry with `npx skills find typescript`, and update all skills with `npx skills update`.

## How Skills Work

Agent skills are reusable instruction sets that extend your coding agent's capabilities and are defined in SKILL.md files with YAML frontmatter containing a name and description.

The latest version can be run with `npx skills@latest` to access the most current features and skill packages available in 2026.

# Skills Organization by Category

Based on the repository content, skills are organized into **four main categories**:

1. **Creative & Design**
2. **Development & Technical**
3. **Enterprise & Communication**
4. **Document Skills**

## How Categories Are Defined

The skills are organized in the `./skills` folder structure, but the page content doesn't explicitly show a dedicated configuration file that defines categories. Instead, categories appear to be:

- **Organizational by folder structure** - Skills are grouped in subfolders within `./skills/`
- **Defined in skill metadata** - Each skill's `SKILL.md` file contains YAML frontmatter with:
  ```yaml
  ---
  name: my-skill-name
  description: A clear description of what this skill does and when to use it
  ---
  ```

## Document Skills Reference

The repository specifically mentions source-available document creation & editing skills in dedicated subfolders:
- `skills/docx` - Word document handling
- `skills/pdf` - PDF handling
- `skills/pptx` - PowerPoint handling
- `skills/xlsx` - Excel handling

These are grouped separately because they power Claude's document capabilities and are source-available (not open source).

## Plugin Marketplace

When using Claude Code, skills can be browsed through plugins like:
- `document-skills` 
- `example-skills`

These represent pre-grouped collections installable via the marketplace, though the exact categorization logic isn't detailed in the provided content.

## Report: Skill Categorization Mechanism

Based on my exploration of both the local repo and upstream anthropics/skills, here's how categorization works:

### **Upstream Pattern: `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`**

The **anthropics/skills** repository uses a explicit categorization file at `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`:

```json
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "name": "document-skills",
      "description": "Collection of document processing suite...",
      "skills": [
        "./skills/xlsx",
        "./skills/docx",
        "./skills/pptx",
        "./skills/pdf"
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "example-skills",
      "description": "Collection of example skills...",
      "skills": [
        "./skills/algorithmic-art",
        "./skills/brand-guidelines",
        ...
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "claude-api",
      "description": "Claude API and SDK documentation...",
      "skills": ["./skills/claude-api"]
    }
  ]
}
```

This file:
- Groups individual skills into named **plugin collections** (e.g., "document-skills", "example-skills", "claude-api")
- Each collection has a `name`, `description`, and list of skill paths
- These categories appear in the `npx skills@latest add` CLI selection UI (as reported in your earlier observation of "Claude Api", "Document Skills", "Example Skills" groupings)

### **Current Repo Status**

This repo currently has **NO** categorization layer:

1. **Structure**: Skills are split into `skills/local/` and `skills/vendor/` (filesystem grouping only)
2. **vendor.yaml**: Tracks upstream sources with optional `series:` field (e.g., `series: fullstack-nextjs`) for subdirectory organization, **but this is only for filesystem layout**, not for user-facing category labels
3. **mkdocs.yml**: Uses hierarchical documentation organization (Local, Vendored, Fullstack Next.js subsection) **for docs only**—this does not affect the `npx skills` CLI discovery
4. **No marketplace metadata**: The repo lacks a `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` file or equivalent category manifest that the CLI would read

### **Concrete Recommendation**

**Create `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`** at the repo root with the following structure:

```json
{
  "name": "daviddwlee84-agent-skills",
  "owner": {
    "name": "David D. W. Lee"
  },
  "metadata": {
    "description": "Personal collection of agent skills",
    "version": "1.0.0"
  },
  "plugins": [
    {
      "name": "project-management",
      "description": "Project memory, TODO tracking, and development workflow organization",
      "source": "./",
      "strict": false,
      "skills": [
        "./skills/local/project-knowledge-harness",
        "./skills/local/agent-history-hygiene"
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "ml-ops",
      "description": "ML experiment tracking, DVC pipelines, and model workflow tools",
      "source": "./",
      "strict": false,
      "skills": [
        "./skills/local/mlflow-tracking",
        "./skills/local/dvc-ml-workflow",
        "./skills/local/marimo-batch-mlflow"
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "fullstack-nextjs-series",
      "description": "Full-stack web development: Next.js, Supabase, shadcn/ui, testing",
      "source": "./",
      "strict": false,
      "skills": [
        "./skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/nextjs",
        "./skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/supabase",
        "./skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/shadcn",
        "./skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/react-best-practices",
        "./skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/vercel-storage",
        "./skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/supabase-postgres-best-practices",
        "./skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/web-design-guidelines",
        "./skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/frontend-design",
        "./skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/webapp-testing"
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "authoring-and-docs",
      "description": "Skill creation, documentation generation, and content authoring",
      "source": "./",
      "strict": false,
      "skills": [
        "./skills/local/skill-author",
        "./skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap",
        "./skills/vendor/skill-creator"
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "notebooks-and-widgets",
      "description": "Interactive notebook environments and widget creation",
      "source": "./",
      "strict": false,
      "skills": [
        "./skills/vendor/marimo-notebook",
        "./skills/vendor/streamlit-to-marimo",
        "./skills/vendor/anywidget"
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "other",
      "description": "Specialized tools and utilities",
      "source": "./",
      "strict": false,
      "skills": [
        "./skills/local/quantatitive-factor-researcher",
        "./skills/local/pueue-job-queue"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Why this works:**
- The `npx skills@latest` CLI reads `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` to populate category groupings in its interactive selection UI
- Each plugin is a visible category tab/section in the selection interface
- The `series:` field in `vendor.yaml` remains useful for filesystem organization (to avoid `.` directory bloat)—it and `marketplace.json` complement each other

**Key differences from current setup:**
- `vendor.yaml` governs **source syncing**; `marketplace.json` governs **user-facing category discovery**
- Both can coexist; they serve different purposes

Sources:
- [anthropics/skills marketplace.json](https://github.com/anthropics/skills/blob/main/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json)
- [vercel-labs/skills (npx skills CLI)](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills)
- [Skills-CLI Guide on Medium](https://medium.com/@jacklandrin/skills-cli-guide-using-npx-skills-to-supercharge-your-ai-agents-38ddf3f0a826)

# Add category groupings to the `npx skills@latest add` selection UI

## Context

When users run `npx skills@latest add anthropics/skills`, the upstream
Anthropic skills repo shows skills grouped under labels like **Claude Api**,
**Document Skills**, **Example Skills**, and **Other** (see the screenshot
the user shared). This repo (`daviddwlee84/agent-skills`) currently presents
all 22 skills as a flat list because the `npx skills` CLI has no metadata
file telling it how to group them.

The user wants the same grouped UX for this repo so picking a subset of
skills to install becomes easier — especially as the repo now spans
unrelated domains (ML, notebooks, fullstack web, skill authoring,
project hygiene, job queues, docs).

## Mechanism — verified

The `npx skills` CLI reads `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` at the repo
root. The upstream file (fetched verbatim from `anthropics/skills`) is:

\```json
{
  "name": "anthropic-agent-skills",
  "owner": { "name": "Keith Lazuka", "email": "klazuka@anthropic.com" },
  "metadata": { "description": "Anthropic example skills", "version": "1.0.0" },
  "plugins": [
    {
      "name": "document-skills",
      "description": "Collection of document processing suite ...",
      "source": "./",
      "strict": false,
      "skills": ["./skills/xlsx", "./skills/docx", "./skills/pptx", "./skills/pdf"]
    },
    { "name": "example-skills", "...": "..." },
    { "name": "claude-api", "...": "..." }
  ]
}
\```

Each `plugins[]` entry becomes one collapsible group in the selection UI.
Skills found on disk but **not** listed under any plugin show up in **Other**
automatically (that's how upstream's `template-skill` ends up under "Other").

## Plan

### 1. Create `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`

Single new file. Source paths are relative to repo root and must match the
on-disk skill directory exactly (the CLI matches by path, not name).

Proposed grouping for this repo's 22 skills:

| Plugin name | Skills |
|---|---|
| `skill-authoring` | `skills/local/skill-author`, `skills/vendor/skill-creator` |
| `project-memory` | `skills/local/project-knowledge-harness`, `skills/local/agent-history-hygiene` |
| `ml-workflow` | `skills/local/mlflow-tracking`, `skills/local/dvc-ml-workflow`, `skills/local/marimo-batch-mlflow`, `skills/local/quantatitive-factor-researcher` |
| `notebooks` | `skills/vendor/marimo-notebook`, `skills/vendor/streamlit-to-marimo`, `skills/vendor/anywidget` |
| `fullstack-nextjs` | the 9 skills under `skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/` |
| `infra-and-docs` | `skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap`, `skills/local/pueue-job-queue` |

(If we leave any skill out of the above, the CLI will surface it under
**Other** automatically — that's a valid escape hatch and matches upstream.)

### 2. Tooling integration (decided via AskUserQuestion)

This decision is pending; see the question after this plan. Options:

- **(A) Hand-edit only.** Document in `CLAUDE.md` that adding/moving a skill
  also requires editing `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`. Simple, but
  drift-prone.
- **(B) Validator only.** Add `scripts/validate-marketplace.sh` (called by
  `make kanban` or a new `make marketplace` target) that asserts every
  on-disk skill is either listed in some plugin or intentionally falls
  through to "Other", and that every listed path exists. No auto-update.
- **(C) Validator + auto-insert.** Extend `scripts/add-vendor.sh` with a
  `--plugin <name>` flag that appends the new skill path into the matching
  plugin in `marketplace.json` (using `jq`/`yq`). Mirror behaviour for
  `cd skills/local && npx skills@latest init` would require a separate
  helper script (e.g. `scripts/add-local-skill.sh`).

Recommendation: **B**. It's the smallest addition that prevents drift
without bloating tooling. Plugins change rarely; hand-editing is fine.

### 3. README + CLAUDE.md updates

- README: short section explaining "Categories shown in the install UI come
  from `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`. Edit it when adding a skill."
- CLAUDE.md: one-line pointer in the existing "Vendor System" / "Commands"
  area saying the same thing, plus the validate command if option B is taken.

## Critical files

- **New:** `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — the only file the CLI cares about
- **New (option B/C only):** `scripts/validate-marketplace.sh`
- **Edit:** `README.md` — document the categories file
- **Edit:** `CLAUDE.md` — one-line workflow note
- **Reference (do not change):** `vendor.yaml` — different purpose
  (governs upstream syncing, not user-facing grouping). The `series:` field
  in `vendor.yaml` is independent of `marketplace.json` plugins.

## Verification

After implementation:

1. `cat .claude-plugin/marketplace.json | jq .` — well-formed JSON.
2. `jq -r '.plugins[].skills[]' .claude-plugin/marketplace.json | xargs -I{} test -f {}/SKILL.md && echo OK`
   — every listed skill path exists on disk.
3. From an unrelated directory, run
   `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills` and confirm the
   selection UI now shows the proposed groups instead of a flat list.
   (This requires the changes to be pushed to `main` first — the CLI
   pulls from the GitHub remote, not the working tree.)
4. Confirm any unlisted skill appears under **Other** as expected.

```

**How much tooling should support the new categories file?**

Options:
- **Validator only (Recommended)** - Add scripts/validate-marketplace.sh + a make target. Asserts every listed skill path exists and warns on on-disk skills missing from any plugin. No auto-update. Categorization stays a hand-edit.
- **Hand-edit only, no tooling** - Just create marketplace.json and document in CLAUDE.md/README that adding a skill requires editing it. Smallest change, most drift-prone.
- **Validator + auto-insert into add-vendor.sh** - Validator above PLUS a --plugin <name> flag on scripts/add-vendor.sh that appends new skill paths into the matching plugin via jq. Also requires a parallel helper for local skills.

**Are the 6 proposed plugin groupings (skill-authoring, project-memory, ml-workflow, notebooks, fullstack-nextjs, infra-and-docs) right, or should I adjust before finalizing?**

Options:
- **Use as proposed (Recommended)** - 6 groups covering all 22 skills. Nothing falls into Other. You can edit the JSON later anytime.
- **Merge infra-and-docs into Other** - Drop the infra-and-docs plugin so mkdocs-site-bootstrap and pueue-job-queue fall under the auto-generated Other group, like upstream's template-skill.
- **Mirror upstream more loosely** - Use just 3 broader groups: local-skills, vendor-skills, fullstack-nextjs. Less curatorial work, less informative UI.


**Answer:** Validator only (Recommended), Use as proposed (Recommended)

# Add category groupings to the `npx skills@latest add` selection UI

## Context

When users run `npx skills@latest add anthropics/skills`, the upstream
Anthropic skills repo shows skills grouped under labels like **Claude Api**,
**Document Skills**, **Example Skills**, and **Other** (see the screenshot
the user shared). This repo (`daviddwlee84/agent-skills`) currently
presents all 22 skills as a flat list because the `npx skills` CLI has no
metadata file telling it how to group them.

Goal: same grouped UX for this repo, so picking a subset of skills to
install becomes easier — especially as it now spans unrelated domains
(ML, notebooks, fullstack web, skill authoring, project hygiene, job
queues, docs).

## Mechanism — verified

The `npx skills` CLI reads `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` at the repo
root. Verified by fetching the file from `anthropics/skills` via
`gh api repos/anthropics/skills/contents/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`.
Top-level shape:

\```json
{
  "name": "<marketplace-id>",
  "owner": { "name": "...", "email": "..." },
  "metadata": { "description": "...", "version": "1.0.0" },
  "plugins": [
    {
      "name": "<group-name>",
      "description": "...",
      "source": "./",
      "strict": false,
      "skills": ["./skills/foo", "./skills/bar"]
    }
  ]
}
\```

Each `plugins[]` entry becomes one collapsible group in the selection UI.
Skills found on disk but **not** listed under any plugin show up under
**Other** automatically (that's how upstream's `template-skill` lands
under "Other"). The CLI matches by path, not name — so the strings under
`skills[]` must exactly match on-disk directories containing `SKILL.md`.

## Plan

### 1. Create `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`

The 6 plugin groupings, covering all 22 skills:

| Plugin | Description | Skill paths |
|---|---|---|
| `skill-authoring` | Author / refactor / evaluate Claude Code skills | `./skills/local/skill-author`, `./skills/vendor/skill-creator` |
| `project-memory` | Project memory, TODO tracking, agent-history hygiene | `./skills/local/project-knowledge-harness`, `./skills/local/agent-history-hygiene` |
| `ml-workflow` | ML experiment tracking, DVC pipelines, batch notebooks, quant research | `./skills/local/mlflow-tracking`, `./skills/local/dvc-ml-workflow`, `./skills/local/marimo-batch-mlflow`, `./skills/local/quantatitive-factor-researcher` |
| `notebooks` | marimo notebooks, streamlit migration, anywidget | `./skills/vendor/marimo-notebook`, `./skills/vendor/streamlit-to-marimo`, `./skills/vendor/anywidget` |
| `fullstack-nextjs` | Next.js + Supabase + shadcn/ui + design + testing series | the 9 dirs under `./skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/` (frontend-design, nextjs, react-best-practices, shadcn, supabase, supabase-postgres-best-practices, vercel-storage, web-design-guidelines, webapp-testing) |
| `infra-and-docs` | Documentation site bootstrap, pueue job queue | `./skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap`, `./skills/local/pueue-job-queue` |

The repo-level `metadata.version` will be `"1.0.0"` and `owner` will use
the existing git config name/email.

### 2. Add `scripts/validate-marketplace.sh`

Plain-bash + `jq` validator (no new deps — `jq` is already used by
`scripts/sync-vendor.sh`). Checks:

1. `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` parses as JSON.
2. Every `plugins[].skills[]` path exists and contains a `SKILL.md`.
3. No path is listed in more than one plugin.
4. Every on-disk `skills/**/SKILL.md` (one or four levels deep, matching
   the discovery rules in `CLAUDE.md`) is either listed in some plugin or
   reported as a warning that it will fall through to **Other**.

Wire it into the `Makefile` as a new `make marketplace` target, and
include it in the existing `make kanban` flow (or a new `make validate`
umbrella) so drift is caught alongside backlog validation.

Exit non-zero on any error (missing file, bad JSON, broken path,
duplicate path); non-zero is acceptable for warnings is configurable via
`--strict` if useful, but default to warn-only so `make marketplace`
stays usable while skills are mid-add.

### 3. Documentation touch-ups

- **`README.md`** — add a short "Categories in the install UI" section
  pointing at `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and the validator command.
- **`CLAUDE.md`** — add one bullet to the Commands section
  (`make marketplace`) and one line in "Vendor System" reminding that
  adding a skill also means editing `marketplace.json` (or accepting the
  "Other" fallback).

## Critical files

- **New:** `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — the only file the CLI reads
- **New:** `scripts/validate-marketplace.sh`
- **Edit:** `Makefile` — add `marketplace` target
- **Edit:** `README.md` — categories section
- **Edit:** `CLAUDE.md` — workflow note + new command bullet
- **Reference (do not change):** `vendor.yaml` — different purpose (governs
  upstream syncing, not user-facing grouping). The `series:` field there
  is independent of `marketplace.json` plugins; both can coexist.

## Verification

After implementation:

1. `jq . .claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — well-formed JSON.
2. `bash scripts/validate-marketplace.sh` — exits 0; no broken paths,
   no duplicates, all 22 skills accounted for.
3. `make marketplace` — invokes the validator and passes.
4. Push the changes to `main`, then from an unrelated directory run
   `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills` and confirm the
   selection UI shows the 6 groups (and an empty/absent **Other**) instead
   of a flat list. The CLI pulls from the GitHub remote, not the working
   tree, so the changes must be pushed first.
5. Sanity check: temporarily remove one path from `marketplace.json`,
   re-run `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills`, confirm
   that skill now appears under **Other** — then revert.

```
